newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Violence erupts in southern Albania, one dead.
newsitem.headline: Violence erupts in southern Albania, one dead.

text.p: Anti-government protesters clashed with security forces outside the main police station in the southern Albanian port of Vlore on Sunday, leaving one person dead and at least 40 injured, officials said.

A doctor at the city hospital said a man in his 40s died of a heart attack after protesters pelted the town's main police station with stones and set a truck on fire. Police responded by shooting into the air and hurling stones back.
One person had serious head injuries.
It was the first death recorded in the Balkan country since the outbreak of violent protests last month by investors who had lost their life savings in failed pyramid schemes.
Demonstrators said the victim was covered in blood when taken to hospital and blamed police for his death.
The doctor said many people had suffered buckshot wounds. One policemen was among those hurt.
Eyewitnesses said protesters eventually left the area two hours after the violence flared. City authorities cut off electricity to the area, leaving streets in darkness.
The witnesses said thousands of protesters had moved on the station after the fifth consecutive day of demonstrations in the city when rumours spread that people had been arrested.
Protesters demanding the resignation of the government had earlier overturned cars in the city and set them on fire.
Some marched out of Vlore to set up roadblocks on the main road linking the city with Tirana to prevent police reinforcements being dispatched from the capital.
After the initial wave of protests last month, mass arrests and the threat of long jail sentences kept protesters off the streets for a time.

But protests resumed last week in Vlore after the collapse of a local investment scheme with about $500 million in debts. Police initially tried to halt the protesters but eventually allowed them to move freely through the town.
Riot police with batons prevented an opposition demonstration on Saturday in Tirana.
